statement: Under 8 Del. C. § 103, the certificate of incorporation is signed by the incorporator(s) and delivered to the office of the Secretary of State with the required fees; the Secretary of State certifies filing by endorsing the word 'Filed' with the date and time on the signed instrument, and that endorsement is the filing date. A filed instrument is effective on its filing date unless it states a later effective date, which may not exceed 90 days after filing.
caveat: Section 103 also covers correction of defective instruments (certificates of correction) and alternative execution; a rejected or defective filing has no effect until a conforming instrument is endorsed 'Filed'. Verify current text and Division filing practice before relying on mechanics.
